predecessors.text: Syria, ruled by the Ba'ath Party since the coup of 8 March 1963

successors.name: Syria
successors.text: Syria less the Israeli-occupied Golan Heights

ledger.x: 1967: Syria, ruled by the neo-Ba'athists, is drawn as the Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row.
9-10 June 1967: Israel takes the Golan Heights.
1972: Cliopatria's Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party row ends and its 'Syria' row begins in 1973 over the same cells.

wars.name: Six-Day War (Syrian front)
wars.outcome: Israel took the Golan Heights from Syria on 9-10 June 1967; the cease-fire line became the 'Purple Line'.

certainty.note: Frontiers follow the French-mandate and armistice lines; the Golan edge is a cease-fire line (the 'Purple Line'), which the Golan page names without a date, and is only as sharp as the line held.
